newsitem.title: TURKEY: New Turkish minister vows to fight against mafia.
newsitem.headline: New Turkish minister vows to fight against mafia.

text.p: Turkey's new Interior Minister Meral Aksener vowed on Monday to fight organised crime as she succeeded a predecessor who resigned amid a scandal linking a top police official with a gangster.
"Our struggle against organised crime, terrorism and drugs will continue," Aksener, Turkey's first woman interior minister, said at a ceremony where she took over from Mehmet Agar.
Agar resigned on Friday in the wake of a crash in which a mobster wanted for political killings and drug dealing died in the same car as a senior security official and a former beauty queen.
An Interior Ministry statement released after Aksener's official appointment said officials were considering a full-scale investigation into the crash.

Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and his deputy Tansu Ciller had both denied any link between the crash and the resignation. But Agar said he resigned to clear the way for a parliamentary investigation.
Deputies are scheduled to discuss alleged links between the state and organised crime on Tuesday and vote on whether to hold an investigation.
According to media reports, Agar stayed in the same hotel as the crash victims in the Aegean resort of Kusadasi shortly before the accident.
A deputy from Ciller's True Path Party (DYP), Sedat Bucak, was also in the car when it crashed in the western town of Susurluk.
He was seriously injured and is being treated in an Istanbul hospital, where members of the well-armed Kurdish tribe which he heads were guarding him.
Speculation about links between the state and the underworld has prompted newspaper calls for a campaign to clean up Turkey.

Parliament speaker Mustafa Kalemli told the mass-circulation daily Milliyet the assembly was under pressure from a public that wanted a "clean Turkey" and was uneasy with MPs hiding behind parliamentary immunity.
